item.title: S&P Acquires Nigerian Rating Agency to Deepen Africa Coverage
item.description: S&P Global Ratings acquired a majority stake in Nigeria-based Agusto & Co. to expand its coverage in Africa, which is seen as underserved by global ratings companies.

item.title: Private Equity Firm Unloads Mental Health Chain Into Muni Market
item.description: A Connecticut-based private equity firm plans to sell a chain of mental health centers and sober-living homes through a deal financed by municipal bonds.

item.title: French Container Giant Says Transpacific Revival Boost Profits
item.description: CMA CGM SA, the world’s third-largest container line, said a surge in Chinese shipments is boosting earnings as US companies pad inventories while President Donald Trump rebuilds a tariff strategy dealt a setback in February by the Supreme Court.

item.title: You’ll Know When to Worry About the Strategic Petroleum Reserve
item.description: How low can it go?

item.title: UK Inflation Fears Ease Again Despite Volatile Oil Prices
item.description: Inflation expectations among UK households have fallen close to levels seen before the Iran war despite the resurgence in global oil and gas prices.

item.title: US Insurers Rally as Stocks Shift from AI Loser to Safe Haven
item.description: US insurance-related stocks rallied Tuesday, pushing an industry gauge to a record, as artificial intelligence concerns drove traders toward defensive parts of the market.

item.title: S&P Global’s Shares Drop as Company Misses Profit Estimates
item.description: S&P Global Inc. posted quarterly results that fell short of analysts’ average estimate, hurt by factors including the US-Iran War making it harder to boost pricing on contracts for its energy data, news and analysis unit.

item.title: EU Stocking Up on Brazil Chicken as Ban on Meat Trade Looms
item.description: World’s top chicken exporter Brazil has seen a surge in shipments to the European Union ahead of a September deadline that could result in a halt in meat trade with the bloc.

item.title: Brady Sells $800 Million of Bonds for Honeywell Spinoff Purchase
item.description: Brady Corp., a maker of signs and labels, sold $800 million of private debt to support its purchase of Honeywell International Inc.’s productivity solutions and services business.

item.title: Ghana Earmarks $429 Million to Buy Gold, Shifting Fiscal Risks
item.description: Ghana has allocated 5 billion cedis ($429 million) to finance gold purchases that boost its foreign-exchange reserves after shifting the program from the central bank to the government, potentially increasing fiscal risks.

item.title: UAE Bond Sales Running at Record Pace Against War Backdrop
item.description: Borrowers from the United Arab Emirates are tapping global bond markets at a record pace as the Middle East conflict rages, with sales up a third so far in 2026 versus year-ago levels.

item.title: US Consumer Confidence Falls on Worse Business, Labor Views
item.description: US consumer confidence fell in July as Americans’ views about current business conditions and the labor market deteriorated.

item.title: E-Commerce Platform GrubMarket Files Confidentially for IPO
item.description: GrubMarket Inc. filed confidentially for a US initial public offering, following a string of acquisitions in the past year.

item.title: Nasdaq 100 Heads for Correction as AI Worries Rattle Investors
item.description: The Nasdaq 100 Index is on track to enter a correction as worries about the eventual payoffs from artificial intelligence investments sour sentiment in the technology giants that have powered most of this year’s stock-market advance.

item.title: Apple Becomes Second Company to Hit $5 Trillion in Market Value
item.description: Apple Inc. became just the second company ever to achieve a $5 trillion market valuation.

item.title: SpaceX Falls 20% Below IPO Price, Erasing $1.2 Trillion Value
item.description: SpaceX shares erased one-fifth of their value since the record setting debut of Elon Musk’s rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company, as investors shunned riskier technology firms.

item.title: Moonshot Seeks More Nvidia Chips for Next AI Model, Report Says
item.description: Chinese startup Moonshot AI is seeking access to more of Nvidia Corp.’s advanced Blackwell chips to train the next version of its model, Kimi K4, The Information reported, citing sources it didn’t name.

item.title: First Brands Bankruptcy: Lawsuits Around Alleged Fraud Seek to Recoup Billions
item.description: The pitch to creditors of bankrupt First Brands goes like this: Stick with us just a while longer, and you’ll get a full recovery as we claw back $2 billion from suing a long list of insiders and business partners who allegedly perpetrated a widespread fraud.

item.title: New Apple TV 4K Box, HomePod mini and Siri AI Smart Home Hub Are Coming
item.description: Apple Inc., after spending years as a laggard in the smart home market, is preparing a dramatic new push into the category with fresh devices and software.

item.title: After Ford Soars 44% on AI Fever, Traders Want Proof It’s Real
item.description: Two months after Ford Motor Co. became the latest old-economy manufacturer to be swept up in the artificial-intelligence rally, investors are looking for proof the enthusiasm was justified.

item.title: Alabama Dog Shelter Sues to Block Data Center Putting 44,000 Animals at Risk
item.description: In Alabama, the pushback against AI data centers is turning into a dog fight.

item.title: US Goods Trade Deficit Narrows as Capital Goods Imports Fall
item.description: The US merchandise-trade deficit narrowed in June as a broad-based decline in imports — including a rare pullback in capital goods — outpaced a slide in exports.

item.title: Brazil Inflation Slowdown Sets Up Another Rate Cut Next Week
item.description: Brazil’s annual inflation slowed much more than expected in early July, likely keeping the central bank on track to delivering another interest rate cut next week.

item.title: Colombia Bonds: Auditor Probes Swap Over Constitutional Concerns
item.description: A Colombian government bond swap last October may have violated constitutional principles by shifting financing costs to future administrations in exchange for short-term liquidity relief, an audit by the comptroller general’s office found.

item.title: Royal Caribbean (RCL) Lowers Yield Forecast as Middle East Turmoil Hits Bookings
item.description: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. trimmed its yield forecast and said it sees a “modest” impact on bookings from geopolitical turmoil.

item.title: OPEC+ Plans Quota-Hikes Pause After September, Delegates Say
item.description: OPEC+ expects to pause oil-production quota hikes after a final increase in September as the group continues to evaluate the fast-changing supply impact of the Iran war, two delegates said.

item.title: US Drivers Are Feeling the Global Diesel Squeeze
item.description: With refining margins near a record, processors are prioritizing the fuel at the expense of gasoline.

item.title: Parlay Bets Are Burning Gamblers as Market Takes Off on Kalshi
item.description: Retail bettors are piling into long-shot multi-leg bets on prediction-market platforms, opening up a lucrative opportunity for sophisticated traders taking the other side.

item.title: US Stocks Drop as Chipmaker Rout Has Nasdaq 100 Near Correction
item.description: The Nasdaq 100 Index was heading into correction territory on Tuesday as a decline in chipmakers dragged tech-focused indexes sharply lower.

item.title: Samsung, SK Hynix Leveraged ETFs Bring Boom-And-Bust to South Korean Investors
item.description: The rush into ETFs tied to the memory-chip makers has boosted market volatility in South Korea
